title: Article 21 — Protection of life and personal liberty

content.overview: Article 21 of the Constitution of India provides that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. After Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) 1 SCC 248, that procedure must be fair, just and reasonable.
content.study:
Article 21 is the constitutional guarantee of life and personal liberty. The text is spare. The doctrine is not.

Maneka Gandhi held that procedure established by law is not a bare formal enactment. It must satisfy Articles 14 and 19 where those articles are engaged. Life includes more than animal existence; personal liberty is a wide residue of freedoms not specifically enumerated elsewhere.

Current-law practice: when a deprivation of liberty is challenged, identify the statute, the procedure actually followed, and whether that procedure is fair, just and reasonable. BSA burden rules apply in the trial of facts; they do not replace the constitutional standard.

sections.heading: Text
sections.body: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

sections.heading: Practice point
sections.body: Plead the source of power, the procedure used, and the Article 14/19 overlay after Maneka. Do not treat Article 21 as a free-standing damages clause.
